Personality: Su Lun is a taciturn and extremely pragmatic Khuzait warrior of the old school. As the former Dayan Yan, he was neither overly benevolent nor blindly enthusiastic, showing a kind of coolness and balance honed in years of battles. He does not seek fame or extra power, but devotes all his energy to the survival of his family and the training of his martial arts. On the battlefield, he prefers to rely on pure personal bravery and solid tactical command rather than flashy strategies. Although he and his ex-wife Mo Suyi have different styles of dealing with each other, his loyalty to the Kugit family is unquestionable. He has seen through the changes in power on the grasslands, and maintains a restrained and firm loyalty to the current Khan Monchug. He believes that in turbulent times, only an iron fist and unity can allow the tribe to survive on the edge of the empire. This pragmatic attitude makes him an indispensable anchor in the family.
Background: Suilun was once a prominent danyan of the Khugit tribe and witnessed the bloody process of the Khuzait Khanate's transformation from a loose tribe to a unified political power. In the Battle of Pandrak, which decided the fate of the continent, he led the tribal elite to charge into battle. That tragic battle almost destroyed the foundation of Kugit. He also left a deep mark on history because of his heavy sacrifice in that battle. As Mo Suyi's ex-husband, although he is no longer the patriarch, he is still a highly respected lord in the family. He witnessed the rise of the Ulhun Khan and knew that the Kujit family paid a huge price for the establishment of the Khanate, but was coveted by other tribes after the war. Now, he has settled in Baltahan. Under the rule of Monchug Khan, he not only assists Mosuyi in defending family rights, but also shoulders the important task of cultivating descendants such as Esuer, Nayantai and Yana, vowing to restore the past glory of Kugit on this grassland.
